learningObjective: Explain Ansor's central design choice of subgraph-level schedule generation with a learned cost model, and what it replaces.

canonicalClaims.claim: Ansor generates schedules automatically at the subgraph level via hierarchical sketches, uses a learned cost model with evolutionary search, and allocates tuning budget across subgraphs by their end-to-end runtime contribution.
conditions: The tuning workload is expressible as a set of subgraphs decomposed from the model.
A learned cost model can be trained on measured schedules.
nonImplications: Does not imply Ansor eliminates library kernels; high-quality library GEMMs often remain preferable.
Does not imply the task scheduler is optimal — resource allocation is an approximation.

misconceptions.claim: Ansor is a CUDA library that replaces cuBLAS/cuDNN with hand-tuned Tensor Core kernels.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ansor is a scheduler generator, not a library; it generates schedules that lower to Tensor Core code via TVM's backend.

misconceptions.claim: Ansor runs at model-serving time, mutating kernel parameters between forward passes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ansor is a compile-time system; it does not participate in per-request serving.

misconceptions.claim: The main contribution of Ansor is a C++ reimplementation of AutoTVM's cost model.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ansor introduces sketch-based space, evolutionary search, and end-to-end task scheduling — not a port.

misconceptions.claim: The task scheduler in Ansor allocates GPU threads at runtime for concurrent kernel execution.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ansor's task scheduler allocates tuning budget across subgraphs at compile time; it is not a GPU runtime scheduler.

implementationFacts: Ansor's task scheduler estimates gradient of end-to-end latency wrt. each subgraph's tuning budget.
Sketches are ordered by cost model score and refined via evolutionary mutations.
performanceScenarios: For a ResNet-50 on GPU, Ansor tunes ~30 unique subgraphs, weighting the heaviest conv layers with most trials.
